prompt: Write a roughly 8,000–10,000 word story about a young guy who grew up in Detroit and learned never to judge a book by its cover but always stay ready to defend himself. Start your story the moment he steps off a bus in New York, recalling the night his dad showed him how to turn household items into weapons. End with him facing a would-be mugger on a city street and deciding between violence and understanding. Include at least two flashbacks to Detroit’s struggling neighborhoods, show his internal conflict over first impressions, and weave in the theme that everyone has a backstory you don’t see at first glance.
